And if you are interested in jumping to some of the details, you can look at the description below to find the thing that interests you the most. As always, I like to start with code.

So let's go to my code space here and take a look at a table I created. The first thing I want to draw your attention to is the allowing customizations. This is not a new property, but we've had to change it a little bit to be more flexible.
So we deprecated the always option and extended it with two new as read only as read write. Whereas the as read only is the same as always.
We also added the to be classified option in order for you to specify that you're not quite done with this classification. In this table here, I have different kinds of fields.

If I try to then make the entry number read or writable, then because it's read only, I'll get an error. So, I cannot make it editable. The same goes for the field that has the to be classified option.
It can also not be made editable. The description field which has the as read write can be made editable on my page customization here.
And of course as before if you specified never you cannot use that field in a page customization. Going back to my table here let's look at some of the other things we have in here.

We have a new property on fields called mask type. The mask type has two options for now. The none and the concealed. The idea here is that you will specify the mask type if you want to conceal some data from the UI.

Not to be confused with the extended data type masked because that has a very different behavior in the UI. We'll see that in a little while. On the extended data types, we added a new option called document.
Document is intended for you to to tell the client that this media is actually a document and should be rendered in portrait mode. We'll also see that in a little while.
For the existing properties, auto format type and auto format expression, we added a new code cup rule that will help you enforce the usage of these properties.

On this page, we talked about the fields that had the mask type concealed. One of them being the sensitive code, another one being the masked amount. I also added here a custom field pin code that is actually using the extended data type masked.
So we can see in a second the difference between these two properties on my page here. I also added some fact boxes. The first fact box is the summary fact box.

So there's a very different behavior between the mask type concealed and the extended data type masked. On the right side here, we see the summary. I haven't started summarizing yet.

You can go try it out yourself. If I wanted to hide it, I would set the visibility. Below this one, we see the flight document. As you can see here, it's rendered in portrait mode, giving me a good view that this is actually a document and not just an image.
Let's go back to code on reports. We added the ability to specify tool tips. Tool tips can give you extra data in your report that will help the users know what this data is about.
And the tool tip will actually be part of the XML data that's in your Word report or Excel report. So let's go check it out. I have a report here. I can preview it.

about all the places where you can use it and where you cannot use it.

If you work with locks, you might find this new method very useful. You can set the lock timeout duration to a certain number of milliseconds. You can also set it to zero, meaning disabling it if you want to.
Of course, I do not recommend that as it would wait indefinitely. If you work with record refs, you might find it easy now to use field names to access the fields.
